# Verify Report — issue-557-openspec-archive-sweep — Slice 1 (PR1) — RE-VERIFIED

**Branch**: `feat/issue-557-s1-archive-sweep-selector` (verified as-is, not switched, not modified)
**Scope**: tasks.md Phases 1-5 only (VCS issueView widening, selector `lib/archive-sweep.mjs`, `archive-logic.mjs`/`archive.mjs` rewire, phase-order allowlist fix, tests). Phases 6-9 out of scope.

## FINAL VERDICT (after re-verification): PASS WITH WARNINGS

CRITICAL-1 is CLOSED (fixed in commit 043e482). WARNING-1 remains OPEN, non-blocking, for maintainer sign-off before PR2.

## Original pass (first verify)
Found CRITICAL-1: `runBackfill` (brain/scripts/archive.mjs) archived every folder in `selection.archivable` unconditionally, even when `selection.complete === false` (some issue read failed) — contradicting design D3 ("the backfill archives nothing... exits 1 listing the unreadable iids") and spec `archive-closed-issue-selection`'s "Selector Reads Are Fail-Closed" requirement. Reproduced with a fake-fs harness: mixed batch (1 readable+archivable folder, 1 unreadable folder) resulted in complete=false but still archived the readable folder before exit 1.
Also found WARNING-1 (BLOCKED_OUTCOMES scope — implementer judgment call, self-flagged, not a spec violation) and 2 SUGGESTIONS (both acceptable documented deviations).
Test results at that time: npm test 3173/3173 pass; archive-sweep.test.mjs 15/15; archive.test.mjs 17/17; phase-order-check.test.mjs 42/42. All green — the CRITICAL finding was a design-conformance gap the existing tests didn't exercise (test 5.4 used a single-folder batch that passed trivially).

## Re-verification (commit 043e482 "fix(archive): refuse to archive on an incomplete selector read (issue #557)")

### Fix mechanism
brain/scripts/archive.mjs:143 wraps the archive loop in `if (selection.complete) { ... }`. When complete===false, the loop that previously ran unconditionally over `selection.archivable` does not execute at all — archivedCount/consolidatedCount/unconsolidatedCount stay 0, no fs.rename/writeFile happens for ANY folder including ones already classified ARCHIVABLE. selectSweep itself is unchanged — the selector still correctly classifies each folder; fail-closed is now enforced at the caller, matching design D3's stated responsibility split.

### Independent re-reproduction (fake-fs, no real filesystem touched)
Same scenario as original finding: entries=['issue-100-ok','issue-900-unreadable'], readIssueState 100->closed/completed, 900->null.
Result against the FIXED code: selection.complete=false, selection.archivable=['issue-100-ok'] (still correctly classified), archivedCount=0 (was 1), renames=[] (was 1 rename), exitCode=1. CRITICAL-1 confirmed CLOSED.

### Test 5.4b coverage assessment
brain/scripts/archive.test.mjs:382-423, "5.4b: mixed batch — one archivable folder alongside one unreadable folder". Uses a genuine TWO-folder batch (901 readable/archivable + 902 unreadable) — materially different from pre-existing test 5.4 (single unreadable folder, passes trivially with or without the gate). 5.4b asserts: complete=false, readFailures=['902'], folder 901 still reports outcome=ARCHIVABLE (proves selector unchanged), archivedCount=0, consolidatedCount=0, unconsolidatedCount=0, renames.length=0, fs.exists(901 dir)=true (not moved), exitCode=1. This is the correct regression test for the class — confirmed non-trivial, targets the exact fixed code path.

### Test results (re-run)
- node --test brain/scripts/archive.test.mjs: 18/18 pass (was 17, +1 for 5.4b)
- npm test full suite: 3174/3174 pass, 0 fail (was 3173, +1)
Both match the apply agent's claim exactly.

### New-violation check
- runSingle (single-changeId path) untouched by the diff — only runBackfill and archive.test.mjs changed. Test 5.8 ("runSingle never touches the VCS") still passes.
- Report shape unchanged on a complete run — reportGroup calls, summary log line, exit-code computation structurally identical; tests 5.5-5.8 all still pass unmodified.
- Diff scope still clean: git diff main...HEAD --stat shows only PR1 files (18 files, fix touches only archive.mjs + archive.test.mjs, both already in scope) + openspec planning docs. No leakage into PR2/PR3/PR4.
- New SUGGESTION-3 (minor, non-blocking): on an incomplete run, a folder classified ARCHIVABLE but held back by the gate isn't individually named in any reportGroup section (those only list non-ARCHIVABLE outcomes) — reader sees the unreadable iid via readFailures but no explicit "held back" note for the archivable one. Not a spec/design violation (failure is surfaced, exit 1, nothing silently dropped). Cosmetic polish suggestion for a future pass.

## Findings summary after re-verification
- CRITICAL-1: CLOSED (043e482)
- WARNING-1 (BLOCKED_OUTCOMES scope): OPEN, non-blocking, carry to maintainer sign-off before PR2
- SUGGESTION-1, SUGGESTION-2 (original documented deviations #1, #3): unchanged, acceptable
- SUGGESTION-3 (new): report doesn't name held-back-archivable folders on incomplete runs — cosmetic

## Recommendation
PR1 is now mergeable from a spec/design-compliance standpoint. WARNING-1 should still be raised with maintainer for explicit sign-off before PR2's real backfill run against ~50 live folders. Does not block PR1 merge. Proceed to sdd-archive for this slice or continue chain to PR2 per chain_strategy: stacked-to-main.

Full report (both passes) written to /home/gandalf/IA/brain/openspec/changes/issue-557-openspec-archive-sweep/verify-report.md
